install.heading: Install
install.intro: Clone the repository and run the installer. By default it installs all Skills for both hosts at the user level.

examples.label: Install for one host only, with --target claude or --target codex.
Install into a project instead of your user directory.
Install selected Skills. Repeat --skill once per Skill.

install.defaultSetNote: The default set installs 109 production-ready Skills. The experimental docs-canvas Skill is listed but not installed unless you select it.

codex.heading: Codex plugins
codex.intro: The Codex Skills are also packaged as 22 Codex plugins, one per upstream Cursor plugin. They are an alternative to install.sh. Do not install the same Skill both ways.
codex.codexHooksNote: The separate codex-hooks plugin adds native Codex Stop hooks. It requires Python 3, and you review and trust its hook scripts before use.

rows.to: Normalized to the format each host supports
Preserved for Claude Code. For Codex, converted to allow_implicit_invocation: false in agents/openai.yaml
Converted to .claude/skills/ for Claude Code and to .agents/skills/ or ~/.codex/skills/ for Codex

boundaries.heading: Compatibility boundaries
items: Ordinary installs use manual fallbacks for Cursor hook workflows. The optional codex-hooks plugin ports some of them to Codex.
Skills that use MCP need the corresponding MCP server configured separately in Claude Code or Codex.
Skills that operate the Cursor SDK or Cursor Cloud Agents still require Cursor credentials and services.
Named Cursor subagents are not registered automatically. Their definitions are bundled under references/cursor-agents/.
Skills that use Cursor Canvas fall back to a standalone HTML artifact when Canvas is unavailable.

pullQuote: Skill instructions and local resources can be converted, but Cursor-specific runtime capabilities are not bundled.
